transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Amy Held.
More than 52 million ballots have already been cast ahead
of Tuesday's midterm elections, according to the University
of Florida's election lab.
And billions of dollars are being spent
on campaign messaging from both parties.
But no single race has been costlier than that
for U.S. Senate in Texas,
where both sides have spent more than a half billion dollars.
The Texas newsroom's Blaise Ganey reports Democrat
James Talarico is polling closely
with Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton.
>> Jeffrey Byrd waited about an hour
to cast his early ballot in Austin.
He's lived there for 23 years
and says he wants a different direction for Texas.
>> Kind of tired of what we've been having to put up with
for the last couple decades.
It'd be nice to see some newer attitudes and ideas
and younger people.
>> Byrd voted for Talarico for U.S. Senate.
Polls show a very close Senate race
in what has been a GOP stronghold.
Paxton is campaigning in deep red parts of the state,
trying to boost voter turnout.
And President Donald Trump appeared
with him last week in Lubbock.
For NPR News, I'm Blaise Ganey in Austin.
>> A federal judge in California is barring the Trump
administration from threatening election workers.
NPR's Jude Joffe Block reports it comes
as federal officials have been escalating their feud
with state ones in California.
>> In recent weeks, federal prosecutors
have warned election officials in California and Washington.
They could be criminally prosecuted
if they don't set aside the ballots of voters
the federal government suspects are likely non-citizens.
A coalition that includes unions
that represent election workers
sued to stop the unprecedented threats.
The San Francisco-based judge acted swiftly.
Within a day, the judge issued a temporary restraining order.
Under that ruling until mid-November,
the Department of Justice
and the Department of Homeland Security
may not threaten election workers
or demand they stop processing registered voters ballots.
Jude Joffe Block, NPR News.
>> Russia's oldest independent newspaper
says it is closing down due to intense state pressure.
As NPR's Charles Maines reports,
it is the latest blow to independent Russian media
amid the war in Ukraine.
>> For more than 30 years,
Novik Gizeta reflected the pro-democratic ideals
of a post-Soviet Russia that mostly fell short of them.
The newspaper was often critical of the Kremlin,
even as that reporting came at a cost.
Several of its journalists, including star investigative
reporter Anna Politkovsky, were murdered over their work.
Novik Gizeta's then editor-in-chief, Demetri Murata,
was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2021
over the paper's defense of press freedoms.
Yet in announcing the closing of staff statements
that amid the war in Ukraine,
the Kremlin had intentionally killed the paper's ability
to survive financially or report without its journalists
violating strict wartime censorship laws.
Charles Maines, NPR News.
>> This is NPR News.
At least one person is dead and six more are injured
after a shooting last night at a Halloween store in California
from member station KQED, Alonso Dabo reports.
>> The shooting took place in Fairfield,
about 45 miles from San Francisco.
City officials say the shooting was likely a targeted incident
and that it is not a, quote, "active shooter event."
Fairfield's mayor, Rick Vaccaro,
offered some words to the community.
>> I would just say to the people of Fairfield
to stand together.
I know it's Halloween, and it's always, you know,
just be aware of, you know, everything around you tonight
and hopefully, you know, it'll be a safe night.
>> Authorities say there were seven victims
with gunshot wounds, including one who was killed,
and the survivors were taken to local hospitals.
The Fairfield Police Department says its detectives
are reviewing footage and other evidence
to identify the shooter.
For NPR News, I'm Alonso Dabo.
>> Iran's Supreme Leader says his country
will respond forcefully if anyone attacks,
according to state media.
This, as the U.S. and Israel say,
they are preparing for a potential return to hostilities
after the midterms.
Iran, meantime, has intensified attacks on ships
trying to cross the Strait of Hormuz.
For the third weekend in a row,
hundreds of thousands of protesters
have taken to the streets across France
over cost of living and education issues.
Protests were mostly peaceful,
but several hundred arrests have been reported so far today.
High school students started rallying last month.
Labor unions and others joined,
inspiring similar rallies in Germany and Italy.
It's "NPR News."

topics.text: Early voting tops 52 million ballots ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections, per University of Florida lab
Texas Senate race between Talarico and Paxton draws record spending and tight polling
Austin voter Jeffrey Byrd explains supporting Talarico for Texas Senate seat
Federal judge in California temporarily bars Trump administration from threatening election workers
Russia's oldest independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta announces closure amid state pressure
Shooting at Fairfield, California Halloween store leaves one dead and six injured
Iran's Supreme Leader vows forceful response to attacks as US and Israel prepare possible renewed hostilities
Hundreds of thousands protest cost of living and education issues across France for third weekend
